title: Capacity prepositioning sketchboard — Jan 25 2027
content:
Purpose
- Quick brain-dump and standing notes for capacity prepositioning and short-term hedging across regions (weekly cadence). Intended to capture current thinking, experiment results, and immediate next steps before formalizing into the playbook.

TL;DR (one-liners)
- West-1: small ongoing spike from a single heavy customer; preposition 40 A100-equivalent slots for 48h window starting Jan 27 to avoid cold-start SLO blips.
- EU-Central: baseline healthy. Increase warm-pool in night window (00:00–06:00 UTC) by 20% to absorb batch inference growth.
- AP-South: testing preemptible-heavy mix (70% preemptible) succeeded for low-latency fallback but had 12% job evictions; tune checkpoint frequency.
- Short-term risk: spot market volatility next 72h for GCP west regions — lean on reserved burst capacity if preemption > 15%.

This week — summary of activity (notes from standup + ad-hoc huddles)
- Mon: Baseline capacity telemetry digested (Rina). Identified model-serving tails at 2–3x expected sequence lengths on the customer A workload.
- Tue: Warm-pool experiment (us-west1) spun up 200 slots with a 20s priming TTL; observed 25% lower first-token latency.
- Wed: Autoscaler change rolled (#812) that uses interarrival variance to scale more aggressively for bursty customers. Canaryed in eu-central-1.
- Thu: Preemptible mix test in ap-south1 — ran 48h; noted increased scheduling churn and small throughput degradation for long-context requests.
- Fri: Rapid incident postmortem for a transient scheduler OOM during a priming wave — rerouted heavy priming to a lower priority queue while root cause tracked.

Incidents and near-misses
- Incident: schedulerOOM-jan21 — triggered during bulk prewarming for a marketing demo. Impact: 8m of elevated 429s in us-west1. Root cause: uncontrolled parallel priming of large KV caches + older kernel fallback path. Mitigation: add per-caller priming rate limiter (hotfix deployed Thu).
- Near-miss: spot-run eviction wave (ap-south1) at 02:12 UTC; autoscale responded but led to short-term queueing. Action: increase grace-duration for long-context jobs by 30s.

Capacity plan & projections (next 14 days)
- Inputs: customer commitments (sales pipe), observed growth (% tokens/day), upcoming marketing demo, known cloud spot events.
- Projection summary: need +420 A100-equivalent hours/day across fleet to maintain SLO; distribution: west-1 +220h, eu-central +120h, ap-south +80h.
- Proposed allocation strategy:
  - Short-window reserve: 40 slots us-west1 (48h), pre-authorized to burst from reserved pool.
  - Night-time buffer: +20% warm-pool eu-central (00:00–06:00 UTC) for 10 days.
  - Preemptible experiment continuation in ap-south (limit to 60% preemptible for next run).
  - Contingency: maintain 10% spare capacity across all regions; convert to dedicated if preemption > 20%.

Experiments & learnings
- Warm-pool TTL tuning (us-west1)
  - hypothesis: short TTL (20s–60s) reduces cold-starts without excessive idle cost.
  - result: 20s TTL showed best first-token improvement for our tail workloads; idle cost increase ~3% vs baseline.
- Preemptible mix (ap-south)
  - hypothesis: 70% preemptible will drop costs ~30% while keeping SLO via faster fallback to warm-pool.
  - result: eviction rate 12% — acceptable for stateless short requests, fragile for long-context kv-heavy runs.
  - next step: tune checkpoint cadence + limit long-context jobs on preemptible nodes.
- Autoscaler interarrival variance heuristic (#812)
  - observation: improves response to spikes but created oscillation for mid-size steady customers.
  - mitigation: add dampening window and min-interval.

Operational playbook changes to propose
- Add per-caller priming rate limiter to avoid parallel KV cache construction.
- Introduce "priming-ticket" that limits concurrent priming per model-version per region.
- Warm-pool TTL defaults: 20s for tail-priority workloads, 60s for mid-priority. Document rationale in playbook.
- Preemptible policy: tag long-context inference jobs as non-preemptible unless explicitly marked test.
- Scheduler memory cap: increase safe-guard to prevent OOM when N concurrent primings > X (TBD).

Decisions taken (during meeting)
- Approve 48h allocation for us-west1 (40 slots) starting Jan 27 — Miguel to finalize API call and billing sign-off.
- Continue ap-south preemptible test but reduce target to 60% preemptible and instrument eviction attribution better — Tom to own.
- Roll autoscaler dampening change into canary on Mon morning; monitor for oscillation — Elena to observe.

Action items (owner — due)
- Miguel Santos — finalize & request burst quota for west-1 reserve (2027-01-26).
- Rina Kaur — update capacity forecast spreadsheet and attach runbook section (2027-01-27).
- Tom Huang — implement eviction attribution logging + reduce preemptible target to 60% in ap-south test (2027-01-28).
- Elena Rodriguez — set up dashboard for autoscaler oscillation metrics and alert (2027-01-27).
- Aisha Patel — draft playbook changes (priming-ticket + warm-pool defaults) for review (2027-01-29).

Open questions / things to investigate
- Is a per-model priming cost cap better than per-caller rate limit? Trade-offs?
- Could we use a staged priming queue that prioritizes small-initialization models first to reduce OOM spikes?
- Would a hybrid reserved/spot bidding algorithm (regional) materially reduce cost while keeping preemption below threshold? Need simulation.

Notes to self / rough tech references
- Related tickets: INF-4923 (prepositioning), INF-5010 (priming rate limiter), INF-5031 (autoscaler dampening).
- Draft PR for autoscaler (#812) – avoid merging to prod until dampening monitored.
- Reminder: update cost model sheet with eviction tax assumptions (10% extra scheduling cost).

Meeting log (raw transcript highlights)
- "If we keep everything stateless on preemptible, we can save a lot — but long context kills us." — Tom
- "We need a conservative bump for the marketing demo, better safe than sorry; I prefer reserved burst for 48h." — Miguel
- "Autoscaler oscillations are subtle; dashboards will help us catch them before customer impact." — Elena

Appendix: Quick metric snapshots (sample windows)
- us-west1: median first-token latency (baseline) 42ms -> warm-pool 28ms (20s TTL), QPS tail 2.1 -> 2.6
- eu-central1: slot utilization night window 72% -> target 85% after +20% warm-pool
- ap-south1: preemptible eviction 12%, mean re-schedule time 38s

End notes
- This is intentionally informal; will convert to a playbook PR once action items close and we have one more week of telemetry.
- If anyone wants to add quick observations, drop inline or ping me (Aisha) in #infra-capacity.
